notes:
On starting this task, the working tree under src/Wakeel.Crypto and tests/Wakeel.Crypto.Tests already carried working implementations for 6 of the 7 crypto-verify.json findings (items 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 of the closeout list), each with a passing test, from earlier work in this same tree: (1) ContainerManifest.KeySalt filled by ContainerWriter.Write from RandomBytes.Next(16) and consumed by ContainerKeySource.SubKey via Hkdf.DeriveKey on both write and read paths, tested by Two_office_key_containers_never_share_a_content_key and A_container_missing_its_key_salt_is_reported_as_damaged. (3) PairingAccept.OpenSessionKey/OpenOfficeKey guard Body is null / empty sealed field with CryptoException(Corrupt), tested by An_answer_with_no_body_reports_corruption_not_a_null_reference. (4) ContainerEntrySource.IsAcceptableName rejects Path.GetInvalidFileNameChars() (wildcard/quote chars), names ending in '/', '.' or ' ', and DOS device names case-insensitively, shared by ContainerReader.ValidateShape, tested by An_entry_name_that_is_not_a_legal_windows_file_name_is_refused. (5) KeyWraps.OpenAsAdmin maps ErrorCode.Tampered from DeviceIdentity.Open to CryptoException(WrongPassword), matching ContainerKeySource.OpenContentKey, tested in KeyWrapTests. (6) ContainerWriter.Write truncates CreatedAt to millisecond precision before building the manifest, tested with a clock carrying sub-millisecond ticks (subMillisecond = Now.AddTicks(1234)). (7) ContainerReader.ReadOne and ExtractTo copy through CopyWithLimit, which throws CryptoException(Tampered) as soon as more bytes than expected.Size have been produced, tested by An_entry_larger_than_the_manifest_declares_is_refused_without_buffering_it_whole.

Item 2 (PairingAccept.EnsureTrusted) was only partially implemented: the phone-public-key check (Body.PhoneCertificate.Body.Ed25519Pub/X25519Pub against the phone's own keys, via a phoneIdentity parameter) was already present and tested (An_issued_certificate_for_different_keys_than_this_phone_is_refused), but the second half of the finding -- verifying that the answer body's own plain Body.OrgId/OfficeId/PcDeviceId fields agree with the embedded PC certificate's OrgId/OfficeId/DeviceId -- was missing entirely; nothing in EnsureTrusted compared those two independent sets of fields (only pc.Body vs. the invitation was checked, never Body vs. pc.Body). I added that comparison in PairingMessages.cs (EnsureTrusted, right after the PC signature check), throwing CryptoException(ErrorCode.BadSignature, "The answer's plain fields disagree with its own certificate.") on any mismatch, and added a new test An_answer_whose_plain_fields_disagree_with_its_own_certificate_is_refused in PairingTests.cs that hand-builds a validly-signed PairingAcceptBody whose top-level OrgId disagrees with its own embedded PC certificate and asserts BadSignature.
